# Recipe — add a service module (a third-party SDK behind an existing framework port)

A **service module** is an optional, out-of-tree UPM package that implements a port the framework
already has, backed by an external SDK — AppLovin MAX behind `IAdsService` (`pf-ads-max`, the first
one), Firebase behind `IAnalyticsProvider`. Only the SKUs that install it resolve it; every other SKU
keeps the shipped fake and never sees the SDK.

The whole tier reduces to one sentence: **the framework must not know a module exists, and a module
must not know a game exists.** Governing text: the service-modules spine, AD-MOD-1..9.

## 0. First, prove it is a module

| What you have | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| An **external-SDK implementation of a port that already exists** | This recipe — a module package. |
| Logic with **no external dependency** | Register it in your SKU installer. No module, no package. |
| A **new port**, a new event type, a new `BootCap`, a new RenderLayer, a new migrator, a new `RegisterMessageBroker<T>` | **Spine change** — route it (`AGENTS.framework.md` §7b) *before* the module is written. |
| A fifth assembly role (§2) | **Spine change** — route it. |

**A module defines no seam.** It may only implement an existing port, occupy the type-erased installer
slot, and replace an existing boot node's implementation (§6). Adding a module that stays inside those
three is **not** a spine change: it adds no framework assembly, reference edge, RenderLayer, event
type or kernel boot node.

A module is **never** inside `com.classicspins.prototype-framework` (every SKU would inherit the SDK)
and **never** under `Assets/<Sku>/` (it would know a game). It is its own package.

## 1. Know which of the two port shapes you have

| Port | Resolution | `port.mode` |
|---|---|---|
| `IAnalyticsProvider` | `FanOutAnalytics` resolves `IEnumerable<IAnalyticsProvider>` | **`additive`** — N providers coexist. |
| `IAdsService`, `IPurchaseService`, most others | Single resolve | **`replacement`** — yours supersedes the fake. |

Replacement is "register later", never "delete the framework's line": SKU installers run after every
framework installer, and in VContainer the later registration wins a single resolve. The superseded
fake stays registered and is never constructed. `port.mode` is also what Doctor reads: two live
`replacement` modules on one port are a conflict, two `additive` ones are the design.

## 2. The package layout — four roles, one gated

```
Packages/com.classicspins.pf-<domain>/
├── package.json            deps: the framework only — NEVER the SDK
├── pf-module.json          the self-description (§3) — the single source of truth
├── Runtime/Core/           ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>.Core     engine-free, ungated
├── Runtime/Sdk/            ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>.Sdk      gated by PF_<SDK>
├── Runtime/                ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>          ungated: installer + Null<Sdk>Bridge
├── Editor/                 ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.<Domain>.Editor   editor-only, ungated, #if inside
└── Tests~/<Module>HeadlessTests/                                            globs Runtime/Core/** only — CI step 5c
```

| Role | Engine | Gated | Holds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `….Core` | free (`noEngineReferences: true`) | no | the port implementation, `I<Sdk>Bridge`, the boot node, the preflight **decision** rules — everything hard |
| `….Sdk` | bound | **yes** — the only one | `<Sdk>Bridge`, the thin shell over the SDK. The **only runtime assembly that names an SDK type**. Also the marker type (below) |
| `…` (runtime) | bound | **no, never** | `<Sdk>Installer : ScriptableObject, IInstaller` and `Null<Sdk>Bridge` |
| `….Editor` | editor-only | no (uses `#if PF_<SDK>`) | the `IModulePreflight` implementation and its **fact gathering** (§8). Mandatory for an SDK-bearing module |

A genuinely empty role may be omitted. **Namespace ≡ assembly name**, as everywhere in the framework.

**Allowed references.** Runtime roles: only `ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.{Application, Domain}`,
`VContainer`, `UniTask`, the module's own assemblies and the SDK's runtime assembly. The Editor role
may add `ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Editor` and the SDK's editor-only assembly. **Never**
`Presentation`, `Views`, `Infrastructure`, `Composition`, and never `Game.*`. No SKU assembly ever
references the SDK's runtime assembly — the module is the one path into the SDK.

**The `Sdk` role is the only define-gated assembly**, and `versionDefines` is what arms it — keyed on
the SDK's UPM package with a minimum-version expression, never a Player Settings symbol:

```jsonc
// Runtime/Sdk/ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Sdk.asmdef
{
  "name": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Sdk",
  "references": [ "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Core", "UniTask", "MaxSdk.Scripts" ],
  "defineConstraints": [ "PF_MAX" ],
  "versionDefines": [ { "name": "com.applovin.mediation.ads", "expression": "8.0.0", "define": "PF_MAX" } ]
}
```

The ungated runtime and Editor roles carry the **same `versionDefines` entry** (so `#if PF_MAX` works
inside them) and **no** `defineConstraints`. The runtime role references the `Sdk` assembly
unconditionally and names its types only under `#if PF_<SDK>`. That edge is legal only because Unity
**drops** a reference to an assembly whose define constraint is unsatisfied instead of failing the
compile — undocumented; verified in `UnityCsReference` `CustomScriptAssembly.cs:568` →
`EditorBuildRules.cs:244, 451-465`. Cite it wherever your code relies on it.

**The marker.** The `Sdk` role declares one empty type named `PfModuleMarker_<DEFINE>` —
`internal static class PfModuleMarker_PF_MAX { }` — in any namespace. The Wizard and Doctor look it up
by reflection to confirm the gated assembly actually compiled; the define is never read from
scripting-define symbols (a `versionDefines` define never appears there).

**The SDK must arrive through UPM.** A `.unitypackage` SDK lands in `Assembly-CSharp`, which no asmdef
assembly can reference, so the edge rule cannot even be expressed. Use the SDK's UPM distribution.

## 3. `pf-module.json` — the module describes itself

At the package root. Schema `pf-module/1`; read by one reader (`ModuleMetadata.Parse`) that returns a
named rejection for a bad file, never a half-read object. `pf-ads-max`'s instance, abridged:

```jsonc
{
  "schema": "pf-module/1",
  "id": "com.classicspins.pf-ads-max",            // == package.json "name" — the drift gate checks it
  "displayName": "Ads — AppLovin MAX",
  "frameworkRange": ">=0.4.0 <0.5.0",              // npm node-semver range, prerelease semantics
  "port": {
    "interface": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Application.IAdsService",
    "mode": "replacement",                         // replacement | additive
    "replacesBootNode": "AdsInit"                  // key REQUIRED; null when no boot node is replaced
  },
  "requires": {                                    // the only block the Wizard WRITES
    "scopedRegistries": [ { "name": "AppLovin MAX Unity", "url": "…", "scopes": [ "com.applovin.mediation.ads", "…" ] } ],
    "dependencies": { "com.applovin.mediation.ads": "8.6.5" }     // EXACT versions, never ranges
  },
  "define": "PF_MAX",                              // the define the Sdk role waits on
  "installer": {
    "type": "ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.MaxAdsInstaller",
    "menu": "PrototypeFramework/Ads/AppLovin MAX Installer",
    "assetPath": "Assets/{sku}/Installers/MaxAdsInstaller.asset"  // {sku} substituted at install
  },
  "manualSteps": [ "AppLovin ▸ Integration Manager → paste the SDK Key", "…" ],   // human zone, shown verbatim
  "docs": "recipes/add-service-module.md"
}
```

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `schema`, `id`, `displayName`, `frameworkRange`, `port`, `requires`, `define`, `installer` | **Required.** `summary`, `source`, `manualSteps`, `docs` are optional. |
| `requires.dependencies` | **Exact pins.** A floating SDK silently changes what the bridge was written against. |
| `frameworkRange` | The one range in the file. UPM treats a dependency version as a minimum and never fails on a breaking framework bump — this is what names it. Advisory while the framework is dev-linked or embedded. |
| `port.mode` | The only field that decides conflict (`replacement`) versus fan-out (`additive`). |
| `define` | Must match the `Sdk` asmdef's `defineConstraints` **and** its `versionDefines` define, and the marker type's suffix. |
| `installer.type` | A class in that namespace, implementing `IInstaller`, compiled by the **ungated** runtime role. |
| `manualSteps` | Everything in the human zone (rule #12): SDK keys, network selection, the installer-asset drop. Displayed, **never performed**. |

`package.json` depends on the framework only. The SDK is declared in `requires`, applied to the
**consumer's** manifest by the Wizard — which is what keeps the framework repo (SKU #0) SDK-free.

## 4. Absence refuses — it never falls back to the fake

The installer assembly is **never gated**. It always registers your port implementation; only the
bridge behind it depends on the define:

```csharp
private static IMaxBridge CreateBridge(ILog log)
{
#if PF_MAX   // an #if edge into the gated Sdk role — cite UnityCsReference (§2)
    return new ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Ads.Max.Sdk.MaxBridge();
#else
    return new NullMaxBridge(log);
#endif
}
```

`Null<Sdk>Bridge` **fails every call as a result, never a throw, and logs the module id** on each
refusal. It must never leave the framework's fake resolved: `FakeAdsService` **auto-rewards**, so
"falling back" would ship free rewards to every player behind one warning line. A gated installer is
equally wrong — the Master-Scene installer asset becomes a missing script and the fake is back.

## 5. The shipped fake is the specification

**Read the implementation you are replacing before you write yours.** Ports carry contracts the
interface does not state, and the fake is where they are written down. Known ones:

| Port | What the interface does not tell you |
|---|---|
| `IAdsService` | Must publish `AdVisibilityChanged` at show-start **and** show-end, the latter in a `finally` so a cancelled/failed show never strands the four subscribers (audio duck, interaction lock, gameplay tick, banner reflow). Must auto-log the outcome via `AdAnalyticsMapping` → `IAnalytics`. `IsReadyAsync` is awaited by `AdsInit` as a readiness probe. |
| `IAnalyticsProvider` | Must never throw. `FanOutAnalytics` catches a throwing provider and **re-queues the event**, so a provider that always throws silently converts live telemetry into an ever-growing buffer. |
| `IPurchaseService` | Grants route through the shipped interpreter; a module must not grant directly. |

If you break one of these, nothing fails loudly — the symptom shows up somewhere else entirely.

**Split the SDK boundary.** `I<Sdk>Bridge` (in `Core`) speaks **primitives only** — no SDK type
crosses it. The state machine (load, show, result mapping, publish ordering) lives in `Core` and runs
under `dotnet test` with a fake bridge; `<Sdk>Bridge` in `Sdk` is thin enough to review by eye, and
nothing else covers it.

## 6. Replacing a boot node — `BootNodeOverride.Replace`

SDK init that must be awaited, can fail meaningfully or needs ordering is tier 2 — but a module never
adds a kernel node. It **replaces** the framework's, from its installer:

```csharp
builder.Register<MaxAdsInitNode>(r => new MaxAdsInitNode(r.Resolve<IMaxBridge>(), …), Lifetime.Singleton);
builder.Register<BootNodeOverride>(
    r => BootNodeOverride.Replace("AdsInit", r.Resolve<MaxAdsInitNode>()), Lifetime.Transient);
```

- **`Id` and `Provides` identical** to the node replaced. A cap that loses its sole provider makes
  `RunUntilAsync` / `RerunFromAsync` complete silently without ever becoming ready.
- **`Required => false`.** A dead SDK never blocks boot or raises an error screen.
- **Register the node as itself, never as `IBootNode`** — that would put a second `AdsInit` in the graph.
- The override is **`Transient`**: VContainer's collection provider rejects a second Singleton
  `BootNodeOverride`; the node inside it is still the singleton above.
- **Two modules may not replace the same node** — a second override for one target is a composition
  error (Doctor names it as the `seam:` fact before Install).
- `port.replacesBootNode` in `pf-module.json` names the target.

> **Held by review, not by a test.** `BootNodeOverride.Replace` checks only that the replacement's
> `Id` is non-empty — not that it equals the target, not `Provides`. Until that framework guard
> lands, the module's own headless tests must pin the node's `Id`, `Provides` and `Required`, and no
> module ships to production.

## 7. Consent — an ads module's SDK owns personalized-ads consent (AD-MOD-9)

Personalized-ads consent is asked, stored and applied by the **SDK's own consent flow**, run inside
the replacement `AdsInit`. `IConsentService` is never its authority.

- The node **does not inject `IConsentService`**; the bridge has **no consent setter**; nothing is
  **written back** (`ChangeConsent` would rerun `AdsInit`).
- It keeps `Requires` on `ConsentResolved`, so the SDK's prompt follows the SKU's own agree gate.
- **No timeout over the interactive flow** — `HardTimeout` must not cut off a player reading a privacy
  prompt. Only non-interactive SDK work may carry an internal timeout.
- Publish `AdVisibilityChanged(true, …)` before the flow and `(false, …)` in a `finally`, so the audio
  duck, interaction lock and tick gate hold while it is on screen — no new subscriber.
- **Rerun-idempotent:** SDK init and the consent flow run **at most once per process**; a later
  `RunAsync` returns the memoized outcome (process lifetime, never UserData). Can-show keys on the
  bridge's own initialized state, never `IBootStatus`.
- Configuring the SDK's flow (e.g. MAX's Integration Manager) is a `manualSteps` entry.

## 8. The build refuses a half-wired install — `IModulePreflight`

**A module ships no build hook.** It never implements `IPreprocessBuildWithReport`; the
`buildhook` grep in `sh Tools/CI/greps.sh source` fails any first-party one outside the framework's
own `Editor/`. Build-time concerns enter through the framework's editor interface instead:

```csharp
// ClassicSpins.PrototypeFramework.Editor.Modules (CS.PF.Editor)
public interface IModulePreflight
{
    string ModuleId { get; }                                          // the pf-module.json id
    IEnumerable<ModulePreflightProblem> Check(BuildTarget target);   // empty == fine
}
```

- The framework's **one** `ModulePreflightBuildHook` discovers every implementation by reflection and
  fails the build with **one** `BuildFailedException` listing every problem, each line prefixed with its
  module id. In an interactive editor a dialog offers each problem's fix action first; under
  `-batchmode` only the throw exists (`DisplayDialog` logs `Canceling DisplayDialog` on 6000.3.12f1),
  so **the throw is the enforcement**.
- **Decisions in `Core`** (`<Module>PreflightRules`, headless-tested row by row); **fact gathering in
  `Editor`** (`BuildTarget`, the SDK's editor-only settings). Call a third-party resolver by
  **reflection only**, so the module compiles where it is not installed.
- **Mandatory for an SDK-bearing module.** In a consumer this throw is the only enforcement that
  crosses into their build — everything else there is advisory.

## 9. Constructor rule

**No defaulted parameters on a container-resolved constructor.** VContainer ignores C# default values
and resolves every parameter, so `ILog log = null` is not "optional" — it is a hard dependency that
happens to be satisfied. Take the parameters and null-check them.

## 10. Installing it in a SKU — `Framework/Setup Wizard ▸ Modules`

Never hand-edit a module's `requires` into a manifest. The Wizard does it from the file:

1. **Add by git URL** — paste the module's URL into the Modules section. This adds **only the module
   package** and ends. After the reload the module is a discovered row, `Partial`.
2. **Install** on that row — writes the scoped registries and the pinned dependencies into
   `Packages/manifest.json` (nothing else: no scene, prefab or asset). Refused, with the reason, on a
   `framework-range:`, `conflict:` or `seam:` fact.
3. **Checklist** — `manualSteps` verbatim, the installer's `menu` path and the substituted
   `assetPath`. Creating the installer asset and dropping it into `RootLifetimeScope`'s game-installer
   slot in the Master Scene is **human zone** (rule #12) — a live editor, never YAML.

**Doctor check 16** renders the same state list: `Ready`, `Partial` with every missing fact by name
(`registry:`, `scope:`, `package:`, `define:`, `installer-asset`, `sku`, `framework-range:`,
`conflict:`, `seam:`), or `Absent`. It **reports and never blocks**. In the framework repo, which
installs no SDK, `pf-ads-max` correctly reads `Partial`.

## 11. Distribution

A module is distributed the way the framework is: git URL
`…?path=/Packages/com.classicspins.pf-<domain>#<slug>/v<version>`. Git tags are repo-global, so a
module tags **`<slug>/v<version>`** (e.g. `ads-max/v0.1.0`); a bare `v<version>` is the framework's
alone. Before a module tag, the framework's own release gates run green (`AGENTS.framework.md` §5c).

## 12. Gate

```sh
cd HeadlessTests && dotnet test              # framework-pure ship gate (module core, drift-gate logic)
sh Tools/CI/module-tests.sh                  # every module's Tests~/*HeadlessTests — CI step 5c
sh Tools/CI/greps.sh source                  # incl. buildhook: no IPreprocessBuildWithReport in a module
Tools/Build/pf-build.sh modules --check      # pf-module.json vs the module's code — CI step 3 drift gate
```

- **`modules --check`** holds the metadata true: `define` ↔ the gated asmdef (and the marker),
  `installer.type` ↔ an `IInstaller` class in the ungated runtime role, `port.interface` ↔ the API
  index, `id` ↔ `package.json`. Exit `0` ok · `1` drift (each line names the module and the field) ·
  `2` a file it cannot read. It sees only modules **inside this repo** — a registry-resolved module in
  a consumer's `Library/PackageCache/` is Doctor check 16's, advisory.
- **5c** globs `Runtime/Core/**` only, so it runs with no SDK installed. Adding a module parameterises
  5c — it never adds a CI step.
- **EditMode** through `Tools/pf/pf-tests <Classes>` only when the module's `Editor` role (or the
  framework's module editor code) changed. Never batchmode locally.
- **One boot smoke** (`pf-gates` has the procedure) for the wiring: an installer registration is only
  provable at runtime — boot once and confirm the resolved implementation is yours and the refusal
  line names your module when the SDK is absent.
- **Say what you skipped**, one line each. The PlayMode suite is CI's. A real ad, and the SDK's
  consent flow, are proven only on a device in a consumer project — the in-editor SDK stub proves
  nothing; report them **unverified**.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| The fake still runs | The installer asset is not in the Master Scene slot, or the installer assembly was gated so the asset is a missing script (§4). |
| Every ad call fails and logs your module id | `Null<Sdk>Bridge` — the define is not armed. Doctor check 16 names the `define:` or `package:` fact; run Install. |
| Doctor shows `define:` although the SDK package resolved | The marker type is missing from the `Sdk` role, or `versionDefines` names another package/version (§2). |
| `modules --check` reports `define` | `pf-module.json` `define` no longer matches the gated asmdef's `defineConstraints`/`versionDefines`, or the marker was renamed. |
| `modules --check` reports `installer.type` | The class was renamed, moved to another namespace, lost `IInstaller`, or sits in the gated role. |
| `modules --check` reports `id` | `pf-module.json` `id` ≠ `package.json` `name` — the Wizard and Doctor would read the module as `Absent`. |
| The build fails with a `BuildFailedException` listing `[<module id>]` lines | Your `IModulePreflight` found a half-wired install — each line says what to fix. |
| `greps.sh source` fails `buildhook` | The module implements `IPreprocessBuildWithReport`; move the check into `IModulePreflight` (§8). |
| Input stays locked / audio stays ducked / the sim never resumes after an ad or the consent prompt | The closing `AdVisibilityChanged(false)` was not published in a `finally` on every exit path. |
| A privacy prompt disappears mid-read, or ads go offline after an unrelated consent change | A timeout over the interactive flow, or init not memoized per process (§7). |
| A deep link or consent rerun silently does nothing | A replaced boot node changed its `Id` or `Provides` (§6). |
| `VContainerException` naming a parameter you thought was optional | A defaulted constructor parameter (§9). |
| `type or namespace <Sdk> not found` in a SKU | A SKU assembly referencing the SDK — only the module's `Sdk` role may. |
